{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer-side review)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — 19 rules assessed

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. The Agreement is, on the whole, strongly aligned with our preferred positions: intellectual property, licence scope, indemnification, assignment and change of control, termination for convenience, transition assistance and data return, warranties, audit rights, renewal mechanics, governing law and insurance all meet the preferred position, and the Agreement affirmatively disclaims exclusivity, non-compete, minimum-volume, MFN and non-solicitation obligations on us (§§ 2.1, 12.3, 7.6). Vendor-side commitments in §§ 7.6 and 12.4 run in our favour and we leave them intact.

Two findings are deviations, and both sit in walk-away territory:

1. **Limitation of liability cap (§ 21) — critical.** The structure of § 21 is good (mutual cap, mutual exclusion of indirect damages, a broad Excluded Claims set covering confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and the other Party's IP). The failure is the cap *base*: it is measured by "Fees," which § 1.5 defines as the "Implementation Fee" only — the one-time USD 12,000 charge in the first Order Form (§ 1.6) — and is further narrowed to the first Order Form. Recurring subscription and service charges are excluded, making the cap illusory at roughly USD 12,000, far below the fallback of twelve months' fees and inside walk-away territory (cap below six months' fees).
2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7) — high.** Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages on us of 15% of annual Fees for **every week** an invoice is late, triggered by a mere ten-day delay. The sum is uncapped and compounding and would rapidly exceed remaining contract value. This fails the fallback (which contemplates only an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees) and is walk-away territory.

Both redlines are minimal and surgical: we change only the cap base in § 21.1 (leaving the carve-outs untouched) and replace the § 7.7 penalty with customary late-payment interest.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.7) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes (§ 7.6) |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |

---

## Walk-away items

We should treat the following as conditions of signature rather than negotiating preferences:

1. **§ 21.1 — illusory liability cap.** Because "Fees" is defined as the USD 12,000 implementation fee under the first Order Form, the effective cap is below six months' fees, which the playbook treats as walk-away. **Proposed redline:** replace the cap base with *the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable under the Agreement and all Order Forms in the preceding twelve months and (b) USD 1,000,000*. Fallback: twelve months' amounts paid or payable, without the USD 1,000,000 floor. The existing § 21.2 exclusions and § 21.3 Excluded Claims remain as drafted.
2. **§ 7.7 — uncapped, compounding liquidated damages against Customer.** 15% of annual Fees per week of late payment is a penalty in walk-away territory and exceeds the fallback (an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees). **Proposed redline:** delete the liquidated-damages mechanic and substitute simple interest at 1% per month on undisputed overdue amounts, aligned with the dispute-withholding protection already in § 7.3.

---

## Next steps

1. Issue the two redlines above to Vendor as a single, short markup, with a covering note explaining that we are changing only the § 21.1 cap base and the § 7.7 late-payment remedy and are otherwise accepting §§ 7 and 21 as drafted.
2. Flag in the note that the § 1.5 definition of "Fees" is the root cause of the cap problem, so that any Vendor counter-proposal addresses the definition or the cap base rather than the carve-outs.
3. Confirm with the business owner the expected twelve-month run-rate spend, so we can validate that the USD 1,000,000 floor is the right ask on this deal.
4. Note for the file (no redline required): ownership of Deliverables under § 14.2 is conditioned on payment of Fees; § 19.4 measures refunds by "Fees paid" rather than "paid or payable" and owes cure "within a reasonable period" rather than a fixed window. These are within market norms and we do not propose to raise them unless the counterparty reopens §§ 14 or 19.
5. Hold signature until both walk-away items are resolved; escalate internally if Vendor declines either.
"}
